thread.title: The Dow Is Soaring 158 Points Because the Pie Looks Bigger

title: The Dow Is Soaring 158 Points Because the Pie Looks Bigger
text:
The Dow Is Soaring 158 Points Because the Pie Looks Bigger By Nov. 21, 2018 11:55 a.m. ET Order Reprints Michael Haddad Text size
Wednesday Windup. Investors are getting into the holiday spirit a day early, as stocks reverse the past two days’ painful losses, helped by gains for tech and oil. Even retail, which entered bear territory, is making a comeback. In today’s Intraday Update , we… …take stock of pre-holiday trading; …examine what could keep lifting the market; and …highlight BJ’s Wholesale Club Holdings (BJ) earnings bounce.
Dessert First
Finally something to be thankful for: All three indexes are in the black as of midday Wednesday.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average is up 157.98, or 0.65%, to 24,623.62, while the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite are also higher.
“The old adage states: ‘The Bears have Thanksgiving, while the Bulls have Christmas,’” writes CFRA’ Sam Stovall. While worries from congressional gridlock to higher interest rates and peak profit growth have weighed on stocks of late, leading to the S&P 500’s third-worst quarter-to-date performance through Nov. 20, if history is any guide “these slumps typically led to end-of-year rallies.” If we get some positive news about trade, earnings revisions, or the Fed, “the vacuum of valuations may have become compelling enough to entice investors to push share prices higher ahead of the new year.”
There’s still reason to think that a Santa rally can happen, even after the selloff this month and October’s scary market action. “On balance, the fundamental backdrop of rising earnings, non-problematic inflation and still relatively low interest rates continue to provide valuation support and the basis for a risk-on bias,” writes U.S. Bank Wealth Management’s Terry Sandven. His year-end target for the S&P 500 is 3000.
The Nasdaq is the star today, however, and its return to strength has helped to soothe some frayed nerves given high-profile losses for the former market leading sector—and the fact that tech is still the biggest weighting in the S&P 500.
Not everyone believes that tech is the sector to place your hopes in, however. Smead Capital Management’s Bill Smead argues that recent headlines about tech’s bad behavior will increase the likelihood of government anti-trust scrutiny, and he has some particularly harsh words for Facebook (FB), which he writes has “used its monopoly in social media to brainwash the masses, violate the public’s long-lost privacy and then claim to not have had any idea what they were doing. In effect, we are a nation of Ed Saverin’s, the buddy of Facebook’s CEO, who almost got swindled out of his share of the company.”
While Facebook may be the new LinkedIn (i.e. a running joke and a platform some people actively eschew), plenty of analysts are still more upbeat about the rest of the FAANGs. Yet it’s not just tech that has to prove itself. As T.D. Ameritrade’s J.J. Kinahan writes, “participants aren’t exactly gobbling up stocks” today. Yes, indexes are up, but given the big drops in recent days, we’re still playing from behind. “What they may be doing is simply keeping some powder dry until after they get some clarity on the U.S.-China tariff situation, which could happen in coming days around a meeting between leaders of the world’s two largest economies.”
It’s hard to underestimate the importance of that last point. The trade war may have been pushed from the top of the headlines by the midterm elections and major volatility, but it still remains a major issue—and a potential turning point. As Tigress Financial’s Ivan Feinseth writes, “I still view any positive forward momentum on trade negotiations with China as a powerful upward catalyst for the market and believe we could see an explosive rally to the upside sometime in the first week in December.”
Wouldn’t that be a nice gift?
Midday Movers
Amazon.com (AMZN) is up 2.6% to $1,535, shrugging off reports of technical issues that exposed some user names and addresses, ahead of what may be the most important long shopping holiday weekend of the year.
BJ’s Wholesale Club is up 14.2% to $22.65 after reporting third-quarter earnings. The discount retailer earned 39 cents a share on revenue of $3.22 billion. Analysts were looking for EPS of 33 cents on revenue of $3.16 billion. It raised full-year guidance, as the company now expects EPS of $1.22 to $1.26, on revenue of $12.65 billion to $12.75 billion. Consensus calls for EPS of $1.21 on revenue of $12.9 billion.
Qualcomm (QCOM) is up 1.7% to $55.88 after getting 56 patent claims from Apple (AAPL) dismissed.
Wix.com (WIX) is up 1% to $86.99 after RBC Capital Markets upgraded it to Outperform.
Yandex (YNDX) is up 5.1% to $25.25 after Jefferies initiated coverage with a Buy rating.
